language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hi, I'm Chip.
Hello, my name is Tu. This rice field has been in my family for many generations.
There is a lot of math involved, like figuring out the surface area of each field to know how much rice I have to plant.
Or the perimeter around the livestock area so I know how much fencing to buy.
Let's start small with this flower bed. The longest side (length) is 5 m and the width (breadth) is 2 m.
To calculate the surface area of a square or rectangle, the formula is LxB. So that makes the area 5 m x 2 m = 10 m<sup>2</sup>
Did you notice that the area is squared? Area is always measured in square measures.
To calculate the distance around, you add up all the sides (L + L + B + B).

The perimeter is:
5 m + 5 m + 2 m + 2 m = 14 m
This is a small example. When the size gets really big, I use these other units of measure:
The Hectare (ha) to measure large areas (like a school or supermarket). 1 ha = 10,000 m<sup>2</sup>

For even larger areas (like towns or states), I use Kilometres (km2).
1 km2 = 1,000,000 m2
You can also look at maps and drawings that are smaller in scale and figure out distances and actual areas.
I think there's an old map of this rice field, so we can see how that works.
